name: TV on the Radio
label: 4AD
lede: An animator and a painter turned a $100-a-month Williamsburg loft into a studio after 9/11, and the records that came out of it ran doo-wop, post-punk and noise through the same wires, with David Bowie singing on one of them.

hero.by: TV on the Radio at Treasure Island, 2014. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Plywood windows, $100 rent
eras.text: Tunde Adebimpe had just quit an animation job and Dave Sitek was selling paintings on the street in SoHo when they started making music in a Williamsburg loft. After September 11 they mostly stayed inside and worked, and by 2003 Kyp Malone had joined and Touch and Go was putting them out.

years.cap: Dave Sitek at WNYU, New York
years.src: Guardian: Tunde Adebimpe · GQ: The Survivors
years.h: An animator and a painter move into a freezing loft
years.p: A friend offered Adebimpe the third floor of a Williamsburg building for $100 a month: plywood on the windows, one lightbulb, a toilet and a sink. He and roommate Sitek started recording there.
years.xp:
Adebimpe told GQ that nobody in the band wanted a job, or could hold one, and that the loft was full of people painting and writing. He had worked as an animator, including on MTV's Celebrity Deathmatch, per the Guardian.

He also told GQ that after September 11 there was "a collective unspoken decision" to stay inside and work on things that meant something, and that the Young Liars songs came out of that time.

years.src: Guardian: Tunde Adebimpe · Wikipedia: TV on the Radio
years.h: OK Calculator gets left in coffee shops
years.p: The self-released debut, its title a nod to [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]]'s OK Computer, was a CD Adebimpe and Sitek left around Williamsburg coffee shops. Sitek's brother Jason Sitek was the early drummer.

years.cap: TV on the Radio at the Siren Music Festival, Coney Island
years.src: Magnet: Sound & Vision · Wikipedia: TV on the Radio
years.h: Kyp Malone makes it a trio
years.p: Malone, from Pittsburgh, joins on guitar and a second lead voice. Jason Sitek's time on drums ends the same year.

years.h: Touch and Go releases Young Liars
years.p: Four songs and a hidden fifth: an a cappella version of the [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]]' "Mr. Grieves." Pitchfork gave it 8.9.

eras.title: From Touch and Go to everybody
eras.text: The first album came out on Touch and Go in America and 4AD abroad, won the Shortlist Prize, and turned a studio project into a touring band. By 2005 Jaleel Bunton and Gerard Smith had joined and Interscope had signed them.

years.h: Desperate Youth, Blood Thirsty Babes
years.p: Recorded at Headgear in Brooklyn in August and September 2003, with [[Antibalas|33c2a158-a788-44e5-81ab-142d544a165b]]' Martin Perna on saxophones and flute. Released by Touch and Go in the US and 4AD elsewhere.
years.xp: The "Staring at the Sun" single, out June 28, 2004, has a shorter intro than the Young Liars version. Pitchfork gave the album 7.8 at the time and 9.2 when it reviewed the 20th-anniversary reissue.

years.h: The Shortlist Music Prize goes to a debut from Brooklyn
years.p: Desperate Youth wins the 2004 Shortlist Prize. The same year brings a second EP, New Health Rock.

years.src: Magnet: Sound & Vision · Wikipedia: TV on the Radio
years.h: Jaleel Bunton and Gerard Smith fill out the band
years.p: Bunton takes drums, guitar and keys and Smith plays bass and keyboards. Magnet reported both came in first as touring players.

years.src: Magnet: Sound & Vision · Wikipedia: Return to Cookie Mountain
years.h: Interscope signs them, and Adebimpe keeps the visuals
years.p: The second album is cut at Stay Gold and Head Gear in Brooklyn. Magnet reported Adebimpe offered to make the band's films himself rather than hand its image to label designers.

eras.title: Bowie on the record, Letterman on TV
eras.text: Return to Cookie Mountain leaked months early and still topped Spin's year. Dear Science two years later topped almost everybody's. Then the band took a break so they could stay friends.

years.h: Cookie Mountain leaks, and Pitchfork loves it anyway
years.p: The album is all over the internet months before release, and Pitchfork praises it before it's officially out.

years.h: [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]] sings backup on "Province"
years.p: 4AD released Return to Cookie Mountain worldwide in July; Interscope had it in the US in September. Spin named it album of the year.
years.xp:
The guest list runs from Bowie to Celebration's Katrina Ford, [[Blonde Redhead|6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219]]'s [[Kazu Makino|de61fcb0-a665-413d-b4eb-c8e123f5fb5b]] on "Hours," [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs|584c04d2-4acc-491b-8a0a-e63133f4bfc4]] guitarist [[Nick Zinner|20dc35ec-6cc1-4c66-98a3-4a6116cb3869]] and two members of [[Antibalas|33c2a158-a788-44e5-81ab-142d544a165b]]. It peaked at No. 41 on the Billboard 200; Pitchfork gave it 9.1 and ranked it second for 2006.

The North American edition added two "Wolf Like Me" B-sides and an [[El-P|d9241f5b-721a-4e08-a25a-acd83ed878cc]] remix of "Hours."

years.h: "Wolf Like Me" on Letterman
years.p: The Late Show performance became the band's calling card online. On the US tour that followed they played covers with [[Peter Murphy|b78346af-e3ce-4b36-a0d5-032414de8a27]] of [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] and [[Trent Reznor|bc880664-6751-4998-984d-ebdbff15d229]].

years.src: GQ: The Survivors · Wikipedia: Dave Sitek
years.h: Adebimpe acts for Jonathan Demme; Sitek produces Scarlett Johansson
years.p: Between records, GQ noted, Adebimpe starred in a Demme film, Rachel Getting Married, and Sitek produced Johansson's Tom Waits album Anywhere I Lay My Head.

years.cap: Treasure Island Music Festival, San Francisco, October 2008
years.src: Wikipedia: Dear Science · Wikipedia: TV on the Radio
years.h: Dear Science tops the year-end lists
years.p: Made at Stay Gold in Brooklyn, it debuted at No. 12, the band's highest chart spot. Rolling Stone, the Guardian, Spin and the Pazz & Jop poll all named it the album of 2008.
years.xp:
Sitek took the title from a note in the studio about science fixing real-world problems. It streamed on the band's Myspace and leaked on September 6, ten days before the digital release.

"Dancing Choose" went on Letterman the night before release; SNL followed in February 2009 with "Golden Age" and "Dancing Choose," and The Colbert Report two days later.

years.src: GQ: The Survivors · Wikipedia: TV on the Radio
years.h: Adebimpe announces a year off
years.p: It ends up being about six and a half months. Malone puts out Rain Machine on ANTI- that month and Sitek makes the Maximum Balloon album.
years.xp: Adebimpe told GQ that by the end of the previous tour it "was just not a pleasant place to be" and they'd all rather be friends than be in a band for a while. Sitek's Maximum Balloon brought in Karen O, David Byrne and both of his bandmates' voices.

eras.title: Nine days after the album
eras.text: The band came back with Nine Types of Light and an hour-long film to go with it. Gerard Smith died of lung cancer nine days after the release. Three years later Seeds was the first record without him.

years.h: Nine Types of Light comes with its own film
years.p: Recorded at Sitek's Federal Prism in Glendale and in Brooklyn, it reached No. 12. Every song got a video, cut together with New Yorkers talking about dreams, love and fame, under Adebimpe's supervision.

years.cap: The band at the Malkin Bowl, Vancouver
years.src: Wikipedia: TV on the Radio · Wikipedia: The National
years.h: Gerard Smith dies at 36
years.p: The band had announced his lung cancer diagnosis in March. That night [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]] dedicated "About Today" to him on stage in Kansas City.
years.xp:
The band's statement called him "our beloved friend and bandmate" and said he died the morning of April 20 after a courageous fight. Smith had played bass and keyboards since 2005.

Bunton moved to bass in the studio, and Jahphet Landis and trombonist Dave "Smoota" Smith joined the touring band.

years.h: They curate All Tomorrow's Parties and debut "Mercy"
years.p: The festival is at Pontins holiday camp in Camber Sands. "Mercy" goes online in July.

years.h: Seeds, on Harvest, is the first album without Smith
years.p: Sitek produced it at his Federal Prism studio in Los Angeles. AllMusic heard "a palpable sense of moving on."

years.h: Red Rocks, on the Seeds tour
years.p: The North American summer run includes Shaky Knees, Boston Calling and a night at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Colorado.

eras.title: Silence, then the wolf again
eras.text: A Madison Square Garden support slot in 2019 left Adebimpe wanting out of music altogether. Five years later the band was back on tour, without Sitek on stage, and Adebimpe had a solo record on Sub Pop.

years.big: "I just never want to do this ever again."
q: It should have been such a high point.
years.h: Opening for Weezer and Pixies at the Garden
years.p: Adebimpe, to the Guardian, on that Madison Square Garden show. He banned himself from music for a while afterwards.
years.xp: He said the band's ties had frayed from touring and too much time in each other's pockets, and that he felt "I think I'm done" with music itself. It was weeks before melodies started coming back, which he compared to clipped weeds growing back.

years.cap: The merch wall at Webster Hall, New York, November 2024
years.h: First shows in five years, and Sitek stays home
years.p: Ten dates are announced with a 20th-anniversary reissue of Desperate Youth. Sitek remains in the band but doesn't tour; Adebimpe: "He's just not touring."

years.h: Adebimpe goes solo on Sub Pop with Thee Black Boltz
years.p: Made in his Silver Lake garage with Wilder Zoby, formerly of Chin Chin, after a run of polite label rejections in 2020. The song "ILY" is for his late sister, Jumoke.

years.cap: Adebimpe at Webster Hall, New York
years.src: Guardian: Tunde Adebimpe · Wikipedia: TV on the Radio
years.h: Four sold-out nights in Islington, then South America and Australia
years.p: The comeback tour runs to the end of 2025 across North America, the UK, South America and Australia, with Bunton now on lead guitar.

yt: "Wolf Like Me" on Jimmy Kimmel Live, 2026
years.h: "Wolf Like Me" turns up in a Spider-Man movie
years.p: The 2006 single opens a scene in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Adebimpe had played Peter Parker's chemistry teacher, Mr. Cobbwell, in Spider-Man: Homecoming.
